title: kv: priority segmentation and hybrid evictor to mitigate fragmentation and spill storms
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: In production workloads we observed tail-latency spikes and high OOM churn when large KV items caused allocator fragmentation and reactive spillover flooded the disk/remote store. This PR introduces a two-pronged approach: (1) priority segmentation of the KV cache to isolate large/pinned entries from latency-sensitive small entries, and (2) a hybrid evictor that combines lightweight size-aware LRU with a background compaction/defragmentation pass and a rate-limited spill scheduler to avoid 'spill storms'.

Summary of changes: Adds a new KV segment abstraction (priority, transient, general), implements a hybrid evictor that prefers evicting from the transient/general segments by size and recency and only triggers spill operations when the spill_budget token bucket allows it, and a background compactor that coalesces free blocks to reduce fragmentation. Also exposes a handful of tunables (segment thresholds, spill_rate_limit, compaction_window) and a health metric set for monitoring fragmentation and spillbackpressure.

Design notes: The segmentation is implemented as a thin wrapper around the existing arena allocator; items are tagged at allocation time based on size and origin (pinned requests mark priority). The hybrid evictor keeps per-segment candidate lists and uses a two-stage decision: first try reclaim within-segment via reclaim windows and local compaction; if insufficient and spill budget remains, schedule a spill request. The compactor runs at low priority and uses epoch marking to avoid stalling fast-path allocations.

Upgrade and rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag kv.hybrid_evictor.enabled with default off for 48h canary. Start with conservative spill_rate_limit=50MB/s and compaction_window=5s, monitor new metrics kv.fragmentation_ratio and kv.spill_backpressure. Rollout steps in checklist.

Checklist: - [x] implement segmentation and allocator hooks - [x] hybrid evictor and token-bucket spill throttling - [x] background compactor with non-blocking epochs - [x] unit + integration tests for eviction ordering and compaction safety - [x] benchmarks (micro and e2e) - [x] metrics and Console dashboard tiles - [x] feature flag for staged rollout

Benchmarks: Microbench against synthetic mixed-size workload (75% small tokens, 25% large KV blobs) shows 30-45% reduction in 95th-percentile allocation latency and 2.1x fewer spill operations under sustained pressure when hybrid evictor is enabled. End-to-end inference tests show 8-12% lower p95 latency for interactive small-token workloads when large cache objects are present.

Related: ENG-5241 (KV reliability), PRs that worked on eviction heuristics and paging, and a follow-up ticket to add eviction visualization in the Console.

release_notes: Introduces KV priority segmentation and a hybrid evictor to reduce fragmentation-driven latency spikes and prevent large spill storms. Exposes kv.hybrid_evictor.enabled, kv.spill_rate_limit, and kv.compaction_window for tuning. Benchmarked to reduce p95 allocation latency and spill count under mixed workloads.
